active_question.title: Validate image-compatible fixed Gemini launcher execution
active_question.summary: The ABI mismatch was corrected and offline compatibility passed, but the single provider task was rejected by a temporary-profile base-revision registration error before container, proxy, credential, or provider use.

current_hypothesis.statement: A fixed launcher built in the exact minimal executor-image runtime will start as the mapped Agent identity and pass the offline bounded worktree/output self-test without changing RelayMe, credentials, or egress policy.
success_criteria: The rebuilt launcher has no unavailable dynamic interpreter or library dependency in the executor image.
The offline rootless self-test starts as the mapped Agent identity, reads its fixed worktree input, writes its bounded output, and requires no network.
failure_criteria: The rebuilt launcher cannot start or cannot access its registered mounts in the exact sandbox.
The correction would require an image, policy, or credential change broader than the fixed deployment-local launcher.
primary_metrics: offline launcher exit status and mapped UID/GID
fixed worktree/output access with network none

active_experiment.purpose: Build and exercise only the fixed provider launcher in the exact rootless executor runtime before any provider request.
active_experiment.design: Record host/image ABI metadata, build the fixed launcher in a matching image stage, and run one offline self-test under the established keep-id, Agent-identity, network-none sandbox with synthetic mounts and no real credential.
active_experiment.backend: existing RelayMe test host rootless Podman
active_experiment.output_ref: deployment-local sanitized ABI and offline self-test evidence
active_experiment.result_summary: Host glibc and Alpine musl loader mismatch was reproduced with a safe ABI probe. A static ARM64 launcher passed the exact offline rootless self-test. The one authorized provider task then failed before container launch with invalid_base_revision because its temporary profile inherited an unrelated repository revision; replay retained the same failure and no proxy or provider request occurred.

findings.summary: With keep-id, Agent-owned mounts are visible as the Agent numeric identity while the image process remains a different primary identity. Protected output writes fail; the current group-writable disposable worktree and existing test file remain writable through a supplementary Agent group.
evidence: Both namespace-map forms were captured from inside the container and from a live keep-id container.
Fresh ordinary and disposable-worktree probes used network none, a read-only root filesystem, no provider material, and confirmed the existing fixed test file behavior.
All temporary containers, worktrees, and outputs were removed.

findings.summary: The fixed Agent-local identity mode paired with keep-id produced the Agent identity inside the rootless container and made both protected mounts writable without adding privilege, network, or client authority.
evidence: Local regression rejects unsupported, unpaired, client-supplied, and brief-supplied identity controls.
The isolated real-host fixed task retained all bounded review artifacts, preserved the source repository, cleaned its worktree/container, and replayed the retained result.
No provider credential, provider egress, or production resource was used.

findings.summary: The first provider-enabled executor acceptance stopped before network use: the fixed Go launcher was dynamically linked for the host and the minimal executor image lacked its dynamic loader. This is a deployment launcher/image compatibility defect, not a RelayMe Core or egress-policy defect.
evidence: The single RelayMe task retained exit code 255 and the bounded error that the fixed launcher could not be executed.
The exact idempotency replay returned the same execution ID and retained reviewable result with no changed files.
The proxy audit recorded only attachment preparation and release for the task, with no CONNECT event; direct network remained unavailable to the sandbox.
The temporary profile, credential copy, scoped client, proxy policy, launcher/image, source fixture, and worktree were removed after the attempt.

findings.summary: A static launcher eliminates the Alpine dynamic-loader incompatibility and passed the exact offline rootless self-test. The one provider-task attempt did not test provider connectivity because the deployment-local profile inherited an invalid base revision from a different repository.
evidence: The safe ABI probe identified the host glibc interpreter as unavailable in Alpine, while the corrected launcher was verified static with no dynamic dependencies.
The offline keep-id/Agent-identity self-test succeeded with network none, a read-only root filesystem, and writable isolated worktree/output mounts.

The one RelayMe task returned invalid_base_revision before container creation; its exact idempotency replay returned the same execution ID, proxy audit contained no attachment or CONNECT, and source Git diff was empty.
The entire temporary provider overlay was removed after the attempt.

candidate_next_experiments.summary: After separately authorizing a new one-shot attempt, bind the temporary provider profile to its own source repository base revision, then repeat the same exact-host test using the already validated static launcher without changing RelayMe Core or broadening the egress policy.
